sehemu: Part II: Members of Parliament, Constituencies and Election of Members
jina: Procedure for election of women Members
maudhui: (1) For purposes of the election of women Members referred to in Article 66(1)(b), political parties which participated in the General Election in accordance with the prescribed procedure and obtained at least five percent of all valid votes cast for Members of Parliament shall propose to the Electoral Commission names of women on the basis of the proportion of votes obtained by each party in the parliamentary election. (2) Notwithstanding subarticle (1), the following shall be deemed to be valid votes for a Member returned unopposed in a constituency: (a) where the party nominated a presidential candidate, the votes cast in that constituency for the presidential candidate of that Member's party; or (b) where the party did not nominate a presidential candidate, fifty-one percent of the votes of all persons registered to vote in that constituency. (3) The names of persons proposed pursuant to subarticle (1) shall be declared by the Electoral Commission as election results after the Commission is satisfied that the relevant provisions of the Constitution and law have been complied with. (4) The list of women candidates submitted to the Electoral Commission by each party for the General Election shall be used by the Commission, after consultation with the party concerned, for the purpose of filling any vacancy in this category of Members arising at any time during the life of Parliament.
